newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sells 19 firms for $42 million.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sells 19 firms for $42 million.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet approved the sale of a luxury hotel and an electric tool maker to foreign buyers for $22.3 million and 11.5 million German marks respectively, a Privatisation Agency official said on Tuesday.
The sales were among 19 privatisation deals worth $42 million agreed late on Monday, the agency's director Vesselin Blagoev told a news conference.
"The cabinet approved the sale of 67 percent of Sheraton Sofia Hotel Balkan to the South Korean Daewoo Corp and the sale of 55 percent of Eltos to Germany's Sparky Trading," Blagoev said.
Under the deal Daewoo also pledged to invest some $5 million in the hotel over the next five years.
Blagoev said Berlin-based Sparky Trading GmbH pledged to settle 2.255 billion levs of outstanding debts of the Lovech-based Eltos and to invest 12 million marks in it.
Eltos produces electric hand drills, metal and wood disc cutters and abrasive machines.
"Sparky Trading holds some 52 percent of the Russian market for electric hand tools," Blagoev said.
Also approved was the sale of 51 percent of the 1700-bed Rila hotel in the Borovets skiing resort for $6.1 million.

The contract is expected to be signed within a week between the Privatisation Agency and the buyer, represented by the Klimati company, which manages the hotel and is part of the local conglomerate Multigroup, Blagoev said.

Among the approved deals was also the sale of 55 percent of a major Bulgarian winery -- Chernomorsko Zlato in the Black Sea town of Pomorie -- for $4.5 million, and of the Diana and Briz hotels in the Black Sea resort of Zlatni Piasatsi.
Briz Hotel will be sold for 58 million levs and Diana Hotel for 100 million levs. The buyers, linked to Russian companies, are expected to invest some 900 million levs in them.
The government was expected to approve on Thursday the sale of a 75 percent stake in the indebted Plama oil refinery to local oil trader Euroenergy.
Multilateral lenders have urged Bulgaria to speed up privatisation, as revenue from sell-offs is seen as a major cash source for the debt-ridden state.
Revenues from privatisation deals signed by the agency by August 31 totalled 16.3 billion levs.
Under the contracts new owners are to pay companies' debts worth 7.5 billion levs and invest 8.2 billion levs in them by the year's end, Blagoev said.
Bulgaria's privatisation programme for this year projects revenues of around twenty billion levs. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 876 032; 981 8569
